brief.query: root opening 0.8 mm on 2 mm sheet steel fillet weld: maximum root gap allowed before backing or buildup is required, and how to correct sheet metal fit-up that opens along the joint
brief.headline: Seam too wide at 20 stations; robot refuses to bridge
brief.what_the_cell_measured: At 20 stations the seam opening exceeded one-pass bridging capacity; widest measured 0.75 mm on 2 mm sheet. Robot refused those stations rather than laying a bead.
brief.what_the_sources_say: Welding instructions for stainless steel [1] recommend maximum root gap of 1 mm, absolute max 1.5 mm for fillet welds. AWS D1.1 [4] states if root opening exceeds 1/16 in (1.6 mm), the fillet weld leg must be increased by the amount of the root opening, or the contractor must demonstrate effective throat. TWI [2] notes excessive penetration occurs when joint gap is too large, and root concavity is more likely with excessively large root gap.
do_now: At each of the 20 stations, measure the actual gap with a feeler gauge and record the value.
If any gap exceeds 1.0 mm, grind the joint to reduce the opening to no more than 1.0 mm before re-running the cell.
If grinding is not feasible, increase the programmed fillet weld leg size by the measured gap amount per AWS D1.1 [4] compensation rule.
Re-run the robotic weld cycle on the adjusted stations.
brief.caveat: The sources paragraph carries figures the cited sources do not contain: 1.6; check it against the numbered sources before acting on it.

brief.headline: Seam too wide at 20 stations - robot refused to weld
brief.what_the_cell_measured: At 20 stations the seam opened wider than one pass can bridge; the widest measured 1.50 mm on 2 mm sheet. The robot refused those stations rather than laying a bead.
brief.what_the_sources_say: Welding Instructions Stainless Steel [1] recommends maximum root gap for fillet welds is 1 mm, absolute max 1.5 mm. Design File [3] states that if root opening exceeds 1/16 in (1.6 mm), the fillet weld leg must be increased or the contractor must demonstrate effective throat; gaps approaching the weld leg size create 'nothin' welds' with zero load capacity. A review of shape imperfections [4] notes excessive penetration occurs when joint gap is too large.
do_now: Measure the actual root gap at the 20 refused stations with a feeler gauge
If gap exceeds 1.0 mm, grind the joint to reduce the opening to no more than 1.0 mm before re-welding
If gap cannot be reduced, increase fillet weld leg size per [1] max 1.5 mm limit or adjust welding procedure to bridge the gap
Re-run the seam at those stations only after fit is within acceptable range

brief.query: root opening 3.8 mm on 2 mm sheet steel fillet weld: maximum root gap allowed before backing or buildup is required, and how to correct sheet metal fit-up that opens along the joint
brief.headline: T-joint gap exceeds single-pass bridging limit on 2mm sheet
brief.what_the_cell_measured: At 20 stations, 20 joints had gaps wider than one pass can bridge; the widest measured 3.75 mm on 2 mm sheet. The cell refused those stations rather than laying a bead across them.
brief.what_the_sources_say: Source [3] states the maximum allowed root gap for fillet welds on stainless steel is recommended 1 mm, max 1.5 mm. Source [4] states the maximum root opening for a prequalified fillet weld in a T-joint for sheet steel 1/8" thick is 1/16". Source [2] notes that under AWS D1.1, a 1/8" maximum root opening applies for V-groove preparation, and section 5.22.4.4 addresses base material recovery to close gaps.
do_now: Grind the largest gaps on the 2 mm sheet to 1.5 mm or less per source [3] recommendation
If gaps remain above 1.5 mm, butter the joint edges with additional weld metal to close the root opening before final pass
Verify gap is within 1.5 mm before proceeding with the fill pass
brief.caveat: Sources do not specify a limit for 2 mm sheet specifically; the 1.5 mm maximum from source [3] is a general recommendation for fillet weld root gaps and may need adaptation for this application.

brief.headline: Seam gap 1.25 mm on 2 mm sheet exceeds single-pass bridging limit
brief.what_the_cell_measured: At 20 stations, the seam opened wider than one pass can bridge; the widest measured 1.25 mm on 2 mm sheet. The cell refused those stations rather than laying a bead across them.
brief.what_the_sources_say: Welding instructions for stainless steel recommend maximum root gap 1.5 mm for fillet welds [1]. AWS D1.1 permits buttering to reduce gap, and if gap is reduced to 1/16" (1.6 mm) or less no weld-size increase is needed [2]. TWI notes excessive root gap causes excess penetration and root concavity; acceptance depends on code [3]. AWS forum states root openings greater than allowed but not more than 20 mm may be corrected by welding to acceptable dimensions prior to joining [4].
do_now: Grind the widest gap stations down to 1.5 mm or less
Re-track the seam at those stations to confirm gap is within 1.5 mm
If gap remains >1.5 mm, apply a buttering pass to reduce the root opening before welding
Re-run the robotic weld pass only after gap is confirmed ≤1.5 mm

brief.query: root opening 2.8 mm on 2 mm sheet steel fillet weld: maximum root gap allowed before backing or buildup is required, and how to correct sheet metal fit-up that opens along the joint
brief.headline: Seam too wide at 20 stations: robot refused to bridge
brief.what_the_cell_measured: At 20 stations, the seam opened wider than one pass can bridge; the widest measured 2.75 mm on 2 mm sheet. The robot refused those stations rather than laying a bead across them.
brief.what_the_sources_say: AWS D1.1 5.22.4.3 allows root openings greater than 5.22.4.1 but not greater than twice the thinner part thickness or 3/4 in. (20 mm), whichever is less, to be corrected by welding to acceptable dimensions prior to joining [1]. The TTBBV stainless welding instructions recommend maximum root gap for fillet welds is 1 mm, max 1.5 mm [2]. AWS forum discussion notes buttering/surfacing can reduce root openings, but procedures must be approved, especially when exceeding design intent [1][3].
do_now: Grind the 2.75 mm wide gaps flat to 1.5 mm or less per TTBBV recommendation [2]
Apply buttering passes to the sheet edges to build up the gap to 1.5 mm or less [1][3]
Re-track the seam and verify the gap is within 1.5 mm before welding [measured]
Document the repair procedure and obtain engineer approval if the gap exceeds original design parameters [1]
brief.caveat: Sources do not specify whether 2.75 mm on 2 mm sheet is within or beyond the 5.22.4.3 limit of twice the thinner part (4 mm); engineer approval may be required if exceeding design intent [1]
